title: GPU Operability Workbench — Dedicated Capacity Controls & Health
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design a consolidated GPU Operability Workbench for Dedicated capacity that surfaces per-pool health, autoscaling controls, and burst configuration in a single, actionable view. The goal is to help platform engineers and SREs diagnose pool-level issues quickly, tune autoscaling and burst policies, and take safe operational actions (drain, resize, emergency-burst). This ticket covers wireframes, high-fidelity prototypes, annotation for engineering handoff, and a review pass with PM/infra/eng stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype includes: health summary bar, time-series panel, active request queue, current batch size distribution, KV cache hit-rate gauge, and topology map
Controls panel allows editing: autoscale target (GPU util %), min/max replicas, cooldown seconds, and burst credits with preview of cost impact
Emergency actions defined and gated: drain-pool, force-burst, fallback-model with clear confirmation flows
Design tokens and component references are supplied (buttons, toggles, charts) with accessible color contrast and keyboard flows
Handoff doc includes CSS vars, accessible color palette, and 2 example telemetry query snippets for backend implementation
decisions: Use a left-rail summary (single line per pool) + right main canvas for focused troubleshooting to preserve console parity with other views
Time-series charts use small-multiples for CPU/GPU utilization, tail latency (p99), queue depth, and batching efficiency rather than a single overlaid chart to reduce visual noise
Autoscale controls are inline editable numeric inputs with immediate preview: simulated throughput & cost delta over 1 hour
Burst settings model credits as a soft resource: display current balance, estimated burn-rate at recent peak RPS, and 'sustain' vs 'burst' mode toggles
Fallback model selection uses tagged model variants (latency-optimized vs cost-optimized) with explicit compatibility checks
feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): prioritize clarity on customer impact — add a small banner showing affected customers on incidents
Infra Eng (Devon Park): telemetry queries look good; request adding a 'last kernel selection' field for debugging quantization regressions
SRE (Nora Patel): confirm that emergency-burst requires cross-check with quota service; add a modal documenting side-effects
Design review (team): reduce bright red use in health bars; adopt amber gradient for degraded states to avoid alarm fatigue
Accessibility reviewer (Jorge Silva): keyboard focus order needs a deterministic path across the left-rail and main canvas; will provide a11y checklist
notes: Goal users: platform engineers, SRE, solutions engineering for customer troubleshooting
Primary metrics: GPU util avg/p95, queue length, p99 latency, batching efficiency, KV cache hit-rate, active replicas, and burst credit balance
Constraints: layout must fit within existing console width (1200px content max) and support horizontal collapse for small screens
Internationalization: all labels prepared for i18n; avoid compound verbs in action buttons (use short verbs: Drain, Burst, Resume)
Privacy: no customer prompt content should be surfaced; only tenant IDs and high-level impacted routes
next_steps: Incorporate Dev/Infra feedback and produce v2 prototype (due 2026-03-17)
Run an internal usability session with two SREs and a platform engineer (target 2026-03-18)
Hand off design tokens and annotated screens to frontend for a spike (GH PR referenced above)
Create acceptance test checklist for QA: visual checks, keyboard nav, autoscale simulation, emergency-burst gating
